en.html:
Quiet.
Small waves coming in, that was all. For once, nothing else was insisting on entering my ears.

Some night. Some stretch of shore.
No sinister presence here. No wind trying to turn the world upside down. No fire roaring away.
Here, the world was keeping quiet.

Here, the world was keeping quiet.

en.html:
Broken only.
I looked again. Still broken. I decided firmly that my eyes were playing tricks, and looked once more. My decision made no difference to the moon.

Earth's treasure, our beautiful satellite, was in pieces.

A full moon... I supposed that was what it ought to have been. Only now it had achieved the condition of a plate dropped on the floor.

...There was one theory about the moon's birth, wasn't there?
All the matter floating around the earth had gathered under gravity, gathered and gathered until, finally, there was the moon—

en.html: True enough. The moon was born, if I remembered what I had heard—◆almost at the same time as the earth. Not hundreds of millions of years ago, then. Billions. Even my wildly excessive figure was not excessive enough. No, however I looked at this place, that ancient earth was not fitting. Then what was the explanation? If we had not come to the time when the moon was still being assembled... ...The future? Was something going to break it in the future? Humanity goes to develop the moon and commits such a world-record blunder that there is no proper moon remaining? Or we choose it for the final battle against aliens—?
en.text:
True enough.
The moon was born, if I remembered what I had heard—◆almost at the same time as the earth. Not hundreds of millions of years ago, then. Billions. Even my wildly excessive figure was not excessive enough.

No, however I looked at this place, that ancient earth was not fitting.

Then what was the explanation?
If we had not come to the time when the moon was still being assembled...

...The future?
Was something going to break it in the future?

Humanity goes to develop the moon and commits such a world-record blunder that there is no proper moon remaining? Or we choose it for the final battle against aliens—?

en.html:
Muramasa was still recovering from her confusion. My own head had already gone off to write science fiction. Probably that was why we took so long to notice.

Someone was there.

A figure walking away, leaving footprints one after another in the sand. I could see only the back, and in this darkness there was not much to go by. A woman, it seemed.

She was going farther from us. Then something must have reached her senses.

Suddenly she turned.
Not good. That much I understood, but what could I do now?

We stood facing one another, some distance between us.

en.html:
An armored warrior suddenly appearing from nowhere—that must have been how it looked from her side. Even so, not the slightest alarm showed in her eyes.
They were quiet like the shore itself. Just that small movement beneath the quiet, like a ripple.

Was she looking far back into the past?
Or looking into her own heart?

From her, not one word. From me, also, nothing would come.
